State Prices and Scarcity

Three states, with probabilities and state prices side by side.

A state price is not a raw probability. It is a probability weighted by marginal utility. A dollar in the scarcest state costs the most. The formula below shows exactly that weighting.

For example, a village usually has plenty of 🍞 bread. In a famine year, bread is very scarce. Money to spend in that year is worth far more than money in a normal year.

qs=πs/Es∑tπt/Etq_s = \frac{\pi_s / E_s}{\sum_t \pi_t / E_t}qs​=∑t​πt​/Et​πs​/Es​​
